question: Should Discord Activity support continue from this stale branch, move to the newer overlapping branch, or be rebuilt as a Canvas-plugin-owned design with fail-closed Activity auth?
rationale: The unresolved choice crosses Canvas plugin ownership, Gateway authorization, credential transport, and operator config shape, so automation can identify defects but should not choose the permanent Activity security boundary.

options.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
options.body: Port Activity config, routing, and bridge behavior to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require explicit credentials or a verifiable launch exchange, remove URL tokens, and bound fanout before merge.

options.title: Continue through the newer branch
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65205 as the working branch only after its conflicts and similar security, compatibility, proof, and availability blockers are resolved.

options.title: Pause Discord Activities
options.body: Leave this feature out of core until maintainers settle whether the capability belongs in Canvas/Discord plugins, ClawHub, or a later hardened integration.

recommendation.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
recommendation.body: Port Activity config, routing, and bridge behavior to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require explicit credentials or a verifiable launch exchange, remove URL tokens, and bound fanout before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The key open decision is the Canvas plugin and Gateway auth boundary, and recent Canvas migration history points most strongly to `steipete`.
